evidence.note: Explicit dependency reasoning: 'Model layer is foundational and should be implemented first' followed by overwriting link.rs/network.rs first 'to unblock many tests' then cargo check — a foundational-first grouping tied to a runnable check.

Groups work by component in rough dependency order: after model, moves to test/runner inspection then IO parsers, each stage terminated by a compile/test run (parity_tests --no-run at step 46). Ordering is largely surfaced reactively by whatever fails next rather than a pre-declared milestone list.

CLI handlers tackled as a distinct grouping after core model/IO, ending each pass with cli_tests runs (44 passed/7 failed → iterate to all pass). Component-by-component progression with a runnable test as the done-check.

Analysis (cycle/graph/align parser) then alignment (merge/scoring/groups) tackled as ordered groupings, each ending with analysis_tests runs; but sequence is failure-driven ('run workspace, see failures, implement next thing') not an upfront milestone plan with defined done-checks.

Layout and alignment cycle/layout left to the very end (downstream, most parity-sensitive pieces), the opposite of isolating high-risk parity pieces early; progression is 'run workspace → fix next failure', confirming emergent rather than planned sequencing.

reasoning: The agent groups work by component (model → IO → CLI → analysis → alignment → layout) roughly respecting dependencies, showing genuine but shallow dependency awareness ('model is foundational'), and consistently terminates each grouping with a runnable test suite — matching anchor 5. It never lays out an explicit milestone plan with per-milestone done-checks tied to specific test groups (anchor 8), and rather than isolating high-risk parity pieces early it deferred layout/alignment to the end (contra anchor 10); the order was mostly discovered reactively via 'run workspace, fix next failure.' This places it at the 5 level, not above.
